---
applyTo: "packages/genui/cli/**"
---

When maintaining `genui a2ui create`, remember that the CLI is shipped inside the `@lynx-js/genui` package and `cli/package.json` remains a nested workspace manifest in the published tarball. Do not use `packages/genui/cli/package.json` for generated-template dependency versions; use the parent `packages/genui/package.json` manifest or another publish-rewritten source so generated apps never keep `workspace:` dependency specifiers.

Keep the local Lynx XML playground daemon, transport controller, bootstrap, and preview runtime owned by `packages/genui/cli`. Its control page must compile the hosted Playground's private `src/shared-ui` barrel and canonical CSS directly into `cli/dist/playground`; do not create a second Playground template or stylesheet, and do not add a runtime package dependency or workspace dependency cycle. Local browser code may import hosted source only through that barrel and must not import `ChatController`, `useConversation`, `conversationRepo`, hosted protocol adapters, or GenUI Server configuration.

Treat UI reuse and runtime reuse as separate decisions. Hosted and Local must render the same stateless React chrome, conversation workspace, transcript, composer, artifact, preview shell, and Examples views. Local-only controls and status styles use the `localAgent*` prefix. Generated artifacts and every Local Examples preview, including edited source, must use the CLI-owned isolated Preview origin; never pass local Lynx XML source to the hosted same-origin `LynxXmlView` path.

Treat the local playground as a two-origin security boundary: the authenticated control API binds to `127.0.0.1:<controlPort>` and the credential-free Preview uses `localhost:<independent dynamic port>`, with both listeners on IPv4 loopback. Preview must reject every Host other than its exact `localhost:<previewPort>`, and the API must reject the Preview Origin, missing credentials, and `Origin: null`. Generated Lynx XML may enter only a newly created sandboxed Preview iframe through a revision-bound, hash-checked, one-shot `postMessage`; never mount it in the control page. Verify CSP and sandbox restrictions with the real Chromium malicious-artifact suite on the default topology, including the explicitly allowed self/blob runtime paths and blocked external network destinations.

Durable playground events must contain only bounded, redacted summaries. Snapshots expose their event sequence, pending approvals, and explicit cursor/truncation metadata; the browser starts SSE from that snapshot sequence. Create a data directory one component at a time with `lstat`, and reject symbolic links in every ancestor and internal component before creating or canonicalizing descendants; never use `realpath` to silently accept a requested symlink path.

Do not treat the cumulative number of transient assistant deltas as an active buffer: transient deltas are delivered and discarded, while only durable events consume the durable turn-log budget. Coalesce consecutive assistant deltas before SSE delivery, flush them before visible non-delta events and the final response, and discard pending text when cancellation, failure, shutdown, or lease loss occurs. Bound the actual Agent queue independently from the single protocol-frame limit. Respect `ServerResponse.write()` backpressure by disconnecting only the slow SSE subscriber; a slow browser must never fail the Agent turn.

Turn deadlines and user cancellation use native cancellation only when the complete protocol handle exists (Codex thread plus turn, or ACP session), then terminate the whole detached process group after a short grace period, with SIGKILL as the final fallback. Claude and partial/pre-session states begin process-group termination immediately. Keep the turn lease revoked before any late event can publish an artifact or affect the next turn. Resolve an ACP permission request cancelled with its turn using the transport cancellation outcome; never record that as a browser user denial.

The control UI owns admission races: retry only structured `409 ACTIVE_TURN_EXISTS` responses, reuse the exact client turn UUID and request body, start at 100 ms, cap delay at 1 second, and stop after 15 seconds. Keep cancellation intent independent of the pending request, and bind the stable header cancel control to explicit conversation and turn IDs so workspace SSE rerenders cannot retarget or lose cancellation.

Agent adapters may use only Codex app-server stdio, Claude bidirectional stream-json, or ACP. Do not add PTY scraping, auto-install, auto-login, bypass flags, or implicit approval. Persist the accepted turn and canonical request hash before spawning, and require an active turn lease before atomically publishing a final response as a Lynx XML revision.

Discover local model choices lazily instead of storing them in Agent descriptors or blocking daemon startup. Use Codex `model/list`, Cursor Agent `--list-models`, and Trae CLI `models --json`; Claude Code remains default-only because it exposes no model-list command. Bound and cache probes, deduplicate concurrent discovery, terminate their detached process groups, and validate every non-empty model against a current catalog before launching. Keep the Local settings controls in one shared PromptComposer pill ordered Agent, Model, Effort; never fall back to a free-form model input.

Keep a bounded native JSON-RPC request-ID table in the protocol reducer. An exact duplicate produces no second semantic event; conflicting reuse produces one terminal protocol error. Map each native approval identity to one stable browser UUID and callback for its turn. The supported Agent set is exactly `codex`, `claude`, `cursor`, and `trae`. Availability comes from executable discovery, authentication checks, declared capabilities, and actual protocol behavior; do not add executable-release allowlists or external evidence gates. Real approval probes must traverse the tarball, Daemon, HTTP/SSE, control UI, and a Playwright user click; never call an adapter response callback directly.

Real browser probes must derive a newly created conversation from the creation response and treat an enabled composer, rather than a replaced form node or an empty prompt's disabled submit button, as UI readiness. A user-denied permission may legitimately leave the Agent turn either completed or failed; require the matching request/resolution IDs, successful decision API, one terminal event, no pending approval, and no orphan process instead of forcing a successful turn status.

When the JSON-RPC request-ID table reaches capacity, preserve every recorded identity, emit one terminal overflow error for the first unseen ID, and ignore every later event. Do not evict old IDs. Real and fake behavior reports are diagnostic output only and must never be consumed by the product runtime.
